# Process tables as the script printed them

Input for `test/unit/server/proc_test.dart`. Each file is the verbatim output of
the process function (`-p`) generated by `crates/sbm_parser/src/script.rs`,
run on the platform it is named after — not typed by hand. The parser reads the
table by header name, so a fixture written to match the parser would only prove
the two agree with each other.

| File | Captured on | Branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linux_procps.txt` | `ubuntu:24.04` | procps `ps -axo` |
| `linux_busybox.txt` | `alpine:3.20` | busybox `ps w`, with PPID and START_ID read from `/proc` |
| `macos.txt` | macOS 27, trimmed to three rows | BSD `ps -axo` |

Neither container shows kernel threads (their PID namespace has none), so those
rows are in the test itself.

To refresh one, build the script (`sbm_parser::script::build_script`) and run it
in the same image, e.g. `docker run --rm -v "$PWD/status.sh:/s.sh:ro" alpine:3.20
sh -c 'sleep 30 & sh -c "sleep  31; :" & sleep 0.2; sh /s.sh -p'`.
